registers.name: CONTROL
registers.description: Control register. Bit 0 stores ENABLE. Bit 1 is a write pulse for SAMPLE_START and always reads back as 0. Bit 2 stores IRQ_ENABLE. Bit 3 is a write pulse for ALERT_CLEAR and always reads back as 0. Other bits read as 0.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.description: Master enable for periodic sampling generation.

fields.name: SAMPLE_START
fields.description: Writing 1 generates a one-cycle sample_req pulse. Readback is always 0.

fields.name: IRQ_ENABLE
fields.description: Enables alert_irq when any IRQ_STATUS bit is set.

fields.name: ALERT_CLEAR
fields.description: Writing 1 clears alert_status and STATUS.alert_pending. Readback is always 0.

registers.name: STATUS
registers.description: Status register. Bit 0 sample_done is sticky until cleared by IRQ_CLEAR bit 1. Bit 1 alert_pending mirrors latched alert_status until cleared by ALERT_CLEAR or IRQ_CLEAR bit 0. Bit 2 adc_valid_seen is sticky until reset. Bit 3 busy is high while a requested sample is pending. Other bits read as 0.

fields.name: sample_done
fields.description: Sticky indication that at least one adc_valid completion occurred since last clear.

fields.name: alert_pending
fields.description: Mirrors latched alert_status until cleared by ALERT_CLEAR or IRQ_CLEAR bit 0.

fields.name: adc_valid_seen
fields.description: Sticky after the first adc_valid sample until reset.

fields.name: busy
fields.description: High while a requested sample is pending.

registers.name: THRESHOLD
registers.description: Threshold compare register. threshold_code is stored in bits [11:0]. Upper bits read as 0.

fields.name: threshold_code
fields.description: Filtered temperature threshold used for alert comparison.

registers.name: LATEST_TEMP
registers.description: Latest filtered temperature register. latest_temp is reported in bits [11:0]. Upper bits read as 0.

fields.name: latest_temp
fields.description: Latest filtered temperature code from the two-sample moving-average path.

registers.name: SAMPLE_COUNT
registers.description: Completed sample count. This register is preserved by ALERT_CLEAR and IRQ_CLEAR and is only cleared by reset. Width is 16 bits.

fields.name: sample_count
fields.description: Number of completed adc_valid samples captured since reset.

registers.name: IRQ_STATUS
registers.description: Sticky interrupt status register. Bit 0 alert. Bit 1 sample_done. Other bits read as 0.

fields.name: alert
fields.description: Sticky alert interrupt source, set when filtered temperature exceeds threshold.

fields.name: sample_done
fields.description: Sticky sample-complete interrupt source, set on each adc_valid completion.

registers.name: IRQ_CLEAR
registers.description: Write-one-to-clear register. Writing bit 0 clears IRQ_STATUS.alert and alert_status. Writing bit 1 clears IRQ_STATUS.sample_done and STATUS.sample_done. Upper bits are ignored. Readback is not required and may read as 0.

fields.name: clear_alert
fields.description: Write 1 to clear irq_status_alert and alert_status.

fields.name: clear_sample_done
fields.description: Write 1 to clear irq_status_sample_done and STATUS.sample_done.

Uses actual RTL package top/filelist and firmware register map evidence.

top.functionality: Integrates a digital temperature monitor controller with a temperature sensor ADC behavioral model so the controller can request samples, receive ADC results, and generate alert indication based on monitored temperature thresholds.
responsibilities: Instantiate the digital controller and analog sensor ADC model.
Connect the controller sample request to the sensor model sample request.
Connect the sensor ADC output code and validity to the controller ADC input and validity.
Expose the digital register interface at the top level with the same widths as the controller.
Expose simulation-visible status outputs from the controller.
Expose the sensor temperature stimulus input and analog supply pins at the top level.
Preserve the analog behavioral model in simulation-oriented assembly while providing a physical/abstract placeholder for downstream handoff.
must_not_drive: temperature status outputs as top-level sources
top.reset_behavior: During reset the integrated system must hold the digital controller in its reset state, suppress normal monitoring activity, and preserve a deterministic default register/status condition until reset is released.
behavior_rules: The controller is the owner of the register interface and all monitor status outputs.
The analog sensor model is the source of ADC code and ADC valid information.
Sample request must originate from the digital controller and be consumed by the sensor model.
The top-level shall not reinterpret or modify the controller register semantics.
The top-level shall not fabricate ADC data or validity; those are driven only by the sensor model.
The analog supplies remain top-level ports for simulation/abstract integration visibility.
top.notes: Minimal SoC wrapper with explicit point-to-point connectivity and simulation/physical assembly separation.

assembly_notes: Retain the analog behavioral model in the simulation filelist.
Provide a physical/abstract placeholder for downstream handoff while preserving the top-level contract.

control_model.control_type: register-driven monitoring with sampled analog conversion handshaking
control_model.register_interface: The top-level digital interface is exposed unchanged from the controller signature.
control_flow: Software or testbench writes and reads the controller register interface.
The digital controller issues a sample request to initiate conversion.
The analog sensor model returns an ADC code together with a validity indication.
The controller updates monitor outputs and alert state based on the received conversion result and programmed threshold.
state_dependencies: Threshold programming affects comparison outcomes after valid sampled data is captured.
Alert behavior depends on sampled temperature code relative to the threshold code.

observable_behaviors: After reset release, controller-visible outputs settle to deterministic defaults before any sample completes.
A register write followed by a register read reflects threshold programming through the exposed digital interface.
A sample request from the controller causes the analog model to produce a temperature-dependent ADC code and validity indication.
When the sampled code is below the programmed threshold, the alert output remains inactive.
When the sampled code crosses above the programmed threshold, the alert output asserts and the alert status reflects the condition.
The alert indication remains visible until the controller-defined clear/reset behavior occurs.

smoke_sequences: Apply reset and verify default readable state.
Program the threshold register and read it back.
Trigger a sample conversion and observe ADC valid handoff.
Drive a below-threshold temperature and confirm no alert.
Drive an above-threshold temperature and confirm alert assertion.
negative_sequences: Assert reset during an active monitoring sequence and verify return to defaults.
Issue read/write activity while reset is active and verify the system remains in reset behavior.
Present temperature changes without a sample request and verify no unintended controller update.
Exercise threshold transitions around the comparison boundary.
coverage_focus: Sample request to ADC valid handshake
Top-level visibility of controller outputs and sensor stimulus

notes: System RTL filelists should include both the digital controller and the analog behavioral model for simulation and the corresponding abstract/placeholder assembly for handoff.
The top-level interface intentionally mirrors the controller register port widths and preserves analog stimulus/supply visibility.
No external bus protocol is assumed beyond the explicit register-style signals provided in the signature.
